title: Over the Pyrenees into Spain
summary: An English writer’s account of a journey made alone in 1865, at her publisher’s suggestion after her earlier book of walks in the south of France. She goes through France to Ariège and the eastern Pyrenees, stays for a time at Ax, crosses on foot and by mule into the valley of Andorra, and goes down by the Seu d’Urgel and Calaf to Barcelona, Manresa, and Cardona. She then travels by rail and diligence to Madrid, Granada, and Alicante, and returns by sea to Barcelona and home by Perpignan and Paris. She writes of inns, guides, priests, peasants, fellow travellers, and plants, and of the hardships and insults a woman travelling by herself met with in Spain. French and Spanish speech is given in the original throughout. The dedication is a “Round Robin” of twenty friends’ names.
